title: Notif Guardian: fix delayed FCM push notifications on Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO (HyperOS)
meta_desc: WhatsApp, Telegram or Gmail notifications only arrive when you open the app on your Xiaomi, Redmi or POCO phone? Notif Guardian finds why and keeps HyperOS from freezing Google Play services, so FCM push notifications arrive on time. Free, open source, no root.
og_title: Notif Guardian: notifications on time on Xiaomi HyperOS
og_desc: HyperOS freezes Google Play services while your screen is off, so messages wait until you unlock. Notif Guardian stops that. Free, open source, no root.
og_alt: Notif Guardian home screen on a Xiaomi phone, next to the headline: Messages on time, even with the screen off.
ld_desc: Keeps Xiaomi HyperOS from freezing Google Play services and messaging apps so WhatsApp, Telegram and Gmail notifications arrive in real time.
h1: Messages on time, even with the screen off.
lede: On Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO phones, WhatsApp, Telegram and Gmail notifications often show up only when you unlock or open the app. Notif Guardian finds out why and keeps HyperOS from holding them back.
release_meta_static: Free and open source. No root, no computer. Android APK for HyperOS.
release_meta: Version {version}, released {date}. Free and open source. No root, no computer.
why_intro: Nearly every app's notifications reach your phone through one connection, kept open by Google Play services. Follow a WhatsApp message on its way to you.
hop1_d: WhatsApp's servers pass it to Google.
hop2_d: Sends it to your phone right away.
hop3_d: Receives it on your phone and wakes the app.
hop4_d: Fetches the message and shows it.
verdict_h: HyperOS freezes Google Play services whenever the screen turns off, and it has no battery setting you could change to stop it.
verdict_g: Notif Guardian keeps Google Play services on HyperOS's exemption list, and puts it back within milliseconds whenever HyperOS removes it.
what_intro: Pick the apps whose notifications matter to you. Guardian watches them and fixes what HyperOS breaks.
f1_d: The one fix HyperOS settings can't do, and the one every app depends on.
f2_d: Running, autostart, battery saver, background activity, frozen or not, at a glance.
f3_t: One tap to the right setting
f3_d: Opens the exact HyperOS screen for each problem instead of making you hunt for it.
f4_t: Tells you when an app gets killed
f4_d: And brings it back with a tap, so you don't miss anything.
f5_d: Shows how late each one arrived, so you can see it working.
f6_d: Reads when a notification arrived, never what it says. Goes online only to check for updates.

install_intro: About ten minutes, once, all on your phone. No computer needed.
s1_p1: Download NotifGuardian above, open it on your phone and allow installing from your browser or file manager. Open the app and turn every row in Guardian is set up green, then tap Add apps.
s1_p2: If Android blocks Notification access because the app "comes from an unknown source": open the app's App info, tap ⋮ at the top right, choose Allow restricted settings, then try again. Android asks this once for any app installed from a downloaded file.
s2_p1: Download GuardianHelper above and install it the same way. It has no icon: it works in the background for Notif Guardian. HyperOS may warn that it's built for an older version of Android; that's expected, because it's the only way the helper can do its job.
s2_p2: If your phone refuses to install it at all, install it from a computer instead: turn on USB debugging and Install via USB in Developer options, connect the phone, and run
s3_p1: Open Keep Google Play services awake and turn every row green:
s3_l1: Allow Modify system settings for the helper
s3_l3: Set the helper's Battery saver to No restrictions
s3_l4: Tap Open helper, confirm Android's review, then Test helper
faq_q1: Why do notifications only arrive when I open the app?
faq_a1: HyperOS freezes Google Play services while the screen is off. Push notifications for almost every app travel through it, so they wait until you unlock. Setting an app's battery saver to "No restrictions" helps that app, but HyperOS offers no such setting for Google Play services. That's the gap Notif Guardian fills.
faq_a2: No, and no computer either: both apps install on the phone, and everything keeps working after reboots. Only if your phone refuses to install the helper do you need a computer, once.
faq_q3: Which phones does it work on?
faq_a3: Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO phones on HyperOS. It's tested on a Redmi Note 14 Pro+ with HyperOS 3. Older MIUI versions may work partly. If something doesn't, tap Share diagnostics in the app and open an issue on GitHub.
faq_a4: Barely. Guardian checks your apps once a minute and reacts when HyperOS changes its list. Keeping Google Play services awake is what every non-Xiaomi Android phone does anyway.
faq_q5: Telegram is still a little late sometimes. Why?
faq_a5: If you're active on Telegram Desktop or Web, Telegram's servers hold back the push to your phone on purpose. The phone delivers it the moment it arrives.
faq_a6: No. It records which app posted a notification and when, never the text. Nothing leaves your phone unless you share a diagnostics file yourself.
